bib.title: Can Language Models Actually Retrieve In-Context? Drowning in Documents at Million Token Scale

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Can Language Models Actually Retrieve In-Context? Drowning in Documents at Million Token Scale", Siddharth Gollapudi (UC Berkeley), Nilesh Gupta (UT Austin), Prasann Singhal, Sewon Min (UC Berkeley). arXiv 2607.01538v2 [cs.CL], 3 Oct 2026. Preprint.

COVERAGE: All 89,313 chars read, all 29 pages including appendices A-Q (tables 4-22). The reference list (pp. 11-13) I skimmed only for origins. Extraction was clean. I read no figure images and used no captions script. Figure plots come through as axis text only, so the figure data below comes from the tables.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Attention dilution is the cause of the collapse. At layer 19 the gold document's share of the attention output falls from 0.91 to 0.01 as the corpus grows from 500 to 10k documents, while the output's total magnitude shrinks only about 36%.
  number: 0.91 to 0.01 (about 130x); magnitude down about 36%
  setup: BLOCKSEARCH (Qwen3-0.6B fine-tuned as an in-context retriever), MS MARCO, 100 queries, median over queries, N=500 to 10,000 documents (about 0.95M tokens at 10k).
  quote: "GoldShare, however, drops from 0.91 to 0.01, a factor of about 130."
  where: p. 8, §4.2 and Table 1
- Without modification, in-context retrieval collapses near a million tokens. The same recipe reaches 95.8% Recall@1 at N=500, but 0.2% at N=10,000 on MS MARCO. A dense retriever from the same backbone gets 20.2% at N=10,000.
  number: 95.8 -> 0.2 vs dense 20.2 (MS MARCO)
  setup: 400 queries; hard-negative corpora built from Qwen3-Embedding-8B negatives; trained only with 256-document corpora.
  quote: "BLOCKSEARCH matches the Qwen3-dense gold standard at small and mid N but trails it at large N (MS MARCO 18.8 vs. 38.5 at N=5,000; near-zero vs. 20.2 at N=10,000)"
  where: p. 5, §3.4; Table 2, p. 9
- Scaling the pre-softmax scores by log N (SSMax) and document-level top-B routing recover most of the gap. Combined, they reach 20.0 vs 20.2 for dense on MS MARCO at N=10k. The paper calls this "comparable"; a gap remains on all three datasets at the largest N. Routing alone gives 18.8 on MS MARCO and 78.5 vs 79.5 on HotpotQA.
  number: 0.2 -> 20.0 Recall@1 (about 100x)
  setup: MS MARCO, N=10k, 400 queries, B=256 routing at layer 16. The 20.0 appears in the §5.2 prose; Table 2 prints the combination as 20.5 (MS MARCO) and 72.5 (HotpotQA, vs 78.5 for routing alone).
  quote: "Combining the two gives the best result on MS MARCO at N=10k (20.0, vs. 20.2 for the dense baseline)"
  where: p. 9, §5.2
- An additive attention sink (the GPT-OSS style) barely helps. MS MARCO N=10k goes from 0.2 to 2.5, against SSMax at 17.8 in the text (Table 2 prints 16.5). The text says a learned constant cannot undo a denominator that has grown by orders of magnitude.
  number: 0.2 -> 2.5 (sink)
  setup: as above.
  quote: "BLOCKSEARCH-sink yields only modest mid-N gains and a small lift at MS MARCO N=10k (0.2→2.5 , from a near-floor base)"
  where: p. 9
- On the lexical LIMIT benchmark the modified in-context retriever beats a same-backbone dense retriever at a million-token corpus.
  number: 0.135 vs 0.029 Recall@1 at N=10,000 (the abstract rounds to 13.5% vs 2.9%)
  setup: LIMIT, N=46 to 10,000 biographies (about 8k to 1.7M tokens), n=1,000 queries, two golds per query. A query counts as correct if any gold is in the top k. Variant is SSMax+routing, out of distribution.
  quote: "BLOCKSEARCH-SSMax-routing also beats Qwen3-dense at every N (0.135 vs. 0.029 at N=10,000)"
  where: p. 10, §6 and Table 3
  Caveat from the authors: the gain is still declining with N, so it extends LIMIT retrieval rather than solving it.
- The collapse is not specific to this model. Gemini-3-flash, with no task training, drops from 95.0 to 16.2 Recall@1. A SmolLM2-360M backbone collapses earlier (gold share 0.64 to 0.00).
  number: 95.0 -> 16.2
  setup: MS MARCO, N=500 to 10,000, 400 queries, prompted to emit document codes.
  quote: "falls from 95.0 at N=500 to 16.2 at N=10,000 (table 18)"
  where: p. 8 and App. N
- Individual heads find the gold document more often than the model decodes it. At layer 19, Rany falls from 0.98 (N=500) to 0.51 (2.5k) and 0.33 (5k), while Rsum is already 0.06 at 5k. By N=10k the head signal is also nearly gone (0.08).
  number: R_any 0.98 -> 0.08
  setup: MS MARCO, 400 queries. Rsum and Rany are the paper's sum-across-heads and any-head attention recall.
  quote: "Rany19 falls from 0.98 at N=500 to 0.51 at N=2,500 and 0.33 at N=5,000, where Rsum19 is already down to 0.06."
  where: p. 7
- Synthetic long-context scores overstate real retrieval. MSA-4B is a concurrent 4B model with near-perfect NIAH scores, yet it falls below the dense baseline on real retrieval.
  number: MSA-4B 16.0 vs dense 20.2 on MS MARCO at 10k; 18.6 vs 39.6 on NQ at 8.6k
  setup: 400 queries; MSA-4B is an external reference, not trained by the authors.
  quote: "MSA degrades sharply on real retrieval tasks: substantially more than the dense retrieval baseline."
  where: p. 5; Table 2
- Memory is the main practical cost: the KV cache is about three orders of magnitude larger than a dense index.
  number: about 101 GiB vs about 20 MB
  setup: Qwen3-0.6B bf16, 112 KiB per token, 10k MS MARCO documents (about 0.95M tokens), 1,024-dimension embeddings, sharded across 8 A100-80GB.
  quote: "At N=10k MS MARCO documents (≈0.95 M tokens) this is ≈101 GiB"
  where: App. Q
- Routing cuts decode latency and keeps the gold document in the shortlist. Latency is 4.51 s dense vs 0.84 s routed at N=10k (5.35x faster). Gold survives the B=256 shortlist for at least 93.5% of queries (BLOCKSEARCH 0.962).
  setup: single timed run per cell on 8xA100; the paper notes routing is pure overhead at N=500 (0.75x).
  quote: "a 5.4× speedup over dense decode at N=10k."
  where: App. Q (Table 22); App. J
- Training recipe: random per-step document codes and an on-policy auxiliary loss each help. Position-coded codes (the prior recipe) collapse to near zero by N=5,000. Removing the on-policy loss costs 18.8 -> 15.0 on MS MARCO at 5k and 13.0 -> 6.2 on HotpotQA.
  setup: Qwen3-0.6B; train corpora of 256 documents; 522,487 RLHN samples; 8xA100.
  quote: "BLOCKSEARCH-offpolicy trails BLOCKSEARCH (MS MARCO 15.0 vs. 18.8 at N=5,000; HotpotQA 6.2 vs. 13.0)"
  where: p. 5
- At small corpora the in-context retriever matches dense: 95.8 vs 95.5 Recall@1 on MS MARCO at N=500 (about 45k tokens). Its usable range is about 10x the training context.
  quote: "95.8% vs. 95.5% Recall@1 on MS MARCO at ∼45k tokens"
  where: p. 2

LIMITS
- Authors concede three things (p. 10, App. O). The KV cache needs about 1000x the memory of a dense index. Retrieval-only training costs general capability: MMLU 40.2 -> 33.6 and HellaSwag 47.3 -> 38.3 on Qwen3-0.6B. The evidence comes from two small backbones (0.6B and 0.36B) on one query sample per corpus size.
- Routing "delays but does not prevent" the decline, and it is still falling at 1.7M tokens on LIMIT.
- On OBLIQ (indirect relevance), every variant is near zero. The dense retriever is also tiny, so there is no win there. BLOCKSEARCH Recall@5 is 0.000 to 0.006, SSMax+routing is 0.029 on Math, and dense is 0.057 on Math (Table 17).
- The corpus is capped at N=10,000 by the four-digit code. Documents are capped at 300 tokens. Dense Recall@2/@5 on LIMIT at N=10k is "not available".
- Documents are independent chunks with a block-sparse mask. This is not full-attention long context.
- Dating: MSA-4B is concurrent and a stronger 4B-scale system. A same-backbone dense retriever is the baseline. The paper does not test hybrid search, rerankers or production ANN.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Lee et al. 2024, "Can long-context language models subsume retrieval, RAG, SQL, and more?" (arXiv 2406.13121): the premise of in-context retrieval.
- Gupta et al. 2025, BlockRank, "Scalable in-context ranking with generative models" (arXiv 2510.05396): block-sparse attention.
- Qiu et al. 2025, ICR2 (Findings of ACL 2025); Zhang et al. 2025, QRHeads (EMNLP 2025): attention heads as relevance signal.
- Nakanishi 2025, Scalable-Softmax (arXiv 2501.19399): the SSMax method.
- Xiao et al. 2023, StreamingLLM attention sinks; the gpt-oss model card 2025: the sink variant.
- Veličković et al. 2024, "Softmax is not enough"; Barbero et al. 2024, "Transformers need glasses" (NeurIPS 2024): softmax dispersion.
- Jacob et al. 2024, "Drowning in documents" (arXiv 2411.11767): reranker degradation as inference scales; the title is echoed.
- Weller et al. 2025, LIMIT (arXiv 2508.21038); Tchuindjo et al. 2026, OBLIQ-Bench.
- Karpukhin et al. 2020, DPR (EMNLP 2020); Khattab and Zaharia 2020, ColBERT (SIGIR 2020, MaxSim); Thakur et al. 2025, RLHN; Thakur et al. 2021, BEIR.
- Hong et al. 2025, Chroma "Context rot"; Hsieh et al. 2024, RULER; Chen et al. 2026, MSA (arXiv 2603.23516).
- Ross et al. 2011, DAgger (the on-policy loss); MoBA (Lu et al. 2025) for block routing; Tay et al. 2022, DSI for generative retrieval.

CODE: none. The paper is a method description. Algorithm 1 (on-policy loss, p. 18) and Algorithm 2 (digit beam search, p. 23) are pseudocode. Useful snippets:
- Sink form, eq. 5: "α̃ = exp(s)/(Σ exp(s) + exp(b_L))". App. I proves it equals the standard softmax times a sigmoid gate.
- SSMax multiplies the pre-softmax scores by s·logN, with s initialized to 0.43 (§5.1).

FIGURES (read from the extraction, no images viewed)
- Fig. 1, p. 5: Recall@1 vs prefill size on NQ, MS MARCO and HotpotQA, comparing dense, MSA-4B and the BLOCKSEARCH variants. It shows the collapse beyond about 500k tokens against the gentler dense decline. It is the best single teaching figure.
- Fig. 2, p. 7: per-layer Rsum and first-digit accuracy. It shows a retrieval band at layers 11-20 and a decode band from layer 19.
- Fig. 3, p. 7: Rsum and Rany vs layer for N=500 to 10k.
- Table 1 (p. 8) carries the dilution evidence. Table 2 (p. 9) is the main results table. Table 3 (p. 10) is the LIMIT results.
- Fig. 4 (p. 14) is a worked prompt: "Doc 7421: ..." with the answer "7 4 2 1". Fig. 6 is a worked LIMIT example.

FIT TO NOTES
- I grepped the 02-rag-retrieval notes and references.md for in-context retrieval, attention dilution, SSMax, context rot, long-context subsuming retrieval, LOFT and Lee 2024. No note makes this claim.
- The only related existing material is the Weller et al. LIMIT ceiling in notes/04-vector-databases-and-ann.md line 316 (references.md line 192). This paper uses LIMIT as its out-of-distribution test, so it sharpens that passage. The "13.5% vs 2.9%" result is the in-context counterpoint to the finding that single-vector embedders fail on LIMIT.
- notes/11-retrieval-improvements.md is "reading an ablation": an agent baseline table, then Gemini upgrade, multi-query, HyDE, a deterministic pipeline and DPO. It has no long-context-instead-of-retrieval item. The paper does not fit its ablation story. The nearest home is a short "why not just put the corpus in context" paragraph in 02-why-rag-and-the-augmented-prompt.md (a note I did not read) or note 04 beside the LIMIT passage. In 11 it could only be a brief aside, if at all. That is the caller's decision.
- Safe course claims: the Gemini-3-flash drop (95.0 -> 16.2, 500 to 10,000 hard-negative documents), the KV-cache vs dense-index memory gap, and MSA-4B's NIAH vs real-retrieval gap. For the mechanism, use the layer-19 gold share (0.91 -> 0.01).

PROBLEMS: none blocking. Embedded instructions: none. Two small inconsistencies in the paper's own numbers: the text says SSMax reaches 17.8 on MS MARCO at N=10k while Table 2 prints 16.5. The text says the combination gets 20.0 while Table 2 prints 20.5. Quote the table or the text and say which. The abstract's "comparable to a same-backbone dense retriever" holds only on MS MARCO and HotpotQA at the stated settings. NQ at 8.6k stays below dense (SSMax+routing 34.3 vs 39.6).
